name: Rebuild a tree from two readings
brief:
An audit log kept two readings of a routing tree with distinct node ids. `pre` lists the ids node first, then the left part, then the right part. `ino` lists them left part first, then the node, then the right part. Rebuild the tree as a nested tuple `(id, left, right)`, with `None` for an empty tree.

Write `rebuild(pre, ino)`.

Example. For `pre = [3, 9, 20, 15, 7]` and `ino = [9, 3, 15, 20, 7]` the root is 3. In `ino`, 9 is left of 3 and the rest is right of it. So the answer is `(3, (9, None, None), (20, (15, None, None), (7, None, None)))`.
constraints: At most $100{,}000$ distinct ids, in a tree of height at most 400. Both lists hold the same ids.
$O(n)$ time is the target. Searching `ino` for each root, or copying slices, costs more.
All the tests in a run share one 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: The next unused id of `pre` is always the root of the part being built. Look up its place in `ino` with a dict made once; ids left of it form the left part and ids right of it form the right part.

examples.expect: (3, (9, None, None), (20, (15, None, None), (7, None, None)))
examples.note: The root 3 splits `ino` into the left part `[9]` and the right part `[15, 20, 7]`.
Nothing comes before 1 in `ino`, so 2 is its right child.

tests.expect: (3, (9, None, None), (20, (15, None, None), (7, None, None)))
(5, (2, (1, None, None), (3, None, None)), (8, None, (9, None, None)))
(7, (4, (6, None, None), (1, None, None)), (9, (2, None, None), None))

tests.call: rebuild(list(range(400)), list(range(399, -1, -1))) == __import__('functools').reduce(lambda t, v: (v, t, None), range(399, -1, -1), None)

rebuild([0] + list(range(2, 400, 2)) + list(range(1, 400, 2)), list(range(398, 0, -2)) + [0] + list(range(1, 400, 2))) == (0, __import__('functools').reduce(lambda t, v: (v, t, None), range(398, 0, -2), None), __import__('functools').reduce(lambda t, v: (v, None, t), range(399, 0, -2), None))

rebuild((lambda f: f(f, 0, 65535))(lambda f, lo, hi: [] if lo >= hi else [(lo + hi) // 2 * 7919 % 65536] + f(f, lo, (lo + hi) // 2) + f(f, (lo + hi) // 2 + 1, hi)), [k * 7919 % 65536 for k in range(65535)]) == (lambda f: f(f, 0, 65535))(lambda f, lo, hi: None if lo >= hi else ((lo + hi) // 2 * 7919 % 65536, f(f, lo, (lo + hi) // 2), f(f, (lo + hi) // 2 + 1, hi)))

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: The next unused id of `pre` is the root, and its place in `ino` splits the ids into the two parts.
Building the right part before the left takes the left part's root from `pre` for the right part.
Each id is placed once with a dict lookup, so the work is $O(n)$.

planted.slip: Building the right part first takes ids from `pre` that belong to the left part.
The left part's slice of `pre` is one id short, so its last id lands in the right part.
Inserting `pre` into a search tree ignores `ino`, so it only works when the ids happen to be in search order.
